root_cause.text: The atmel-tdes driver incorrectly used dma_sync_single_for_device() on the output DMA buffer (dd->dma_addr_out) before CPU-side copying in atmel_tdes_crypt_pdc_stop() and atmel_tdes_crypt_dma_stop(), so DMA-written data was not properly synchronized for CPU access on non-coherent systems.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces dma_sync_single_for_device(dd->dev, dd->dma_addr_out, dd->dma_size, DMA_FROM_DEVICE) with dma_sync_single_for_cpu(...) in both stop paths immediately before the comment "/* copy data */", and the CVE/commit message states that using the wrong direction can return stale cache data on non-coherent platforms.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use dma_sync_single_for_cpu() on the DMA output buffer before copying data so the CPU sees the completed device-written data correctly.
intent_record.what: In the non-scatterlist branch of atmel_tdes_crypt_pdc_stop(), the code replaces a call to dma_sync_single_for_device(dd->dev, dd->dma_addr_out, dd->dma_size, DMA_FROM_DEVICE) with dma_sync_single_for_cpu(dd->dev, dd->dma_addr_out, dd->dma_size, DMA_FROM_DEVICE), keeping the same arguments otherwise.
intent_record.how: This changes the DMA buffer synchronization direction after a DMA-from-device transfer completes so the CPU, rather than the device, is given coherent access to the output buffer before the subsequent data copy. It fixes stale or incorrect data being read by the CPU from the DMA destination buffer.

candidates.rationale: This is the incorrect DMA synchronization API used on the output buffer after device DMA completion and before CPU-side copying. For a device-written buffer, syncing for device access does not make the completed data visible to the CPU on non-coherent systems.

This identical statement in the other completion path has the same bug: it prepares the buffer for device access instead of CPU access, so subsequent CPU copying may read stale data from the DMA output buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses the device-direction DMA sync API on the output buffer after DMA completion and before CPU-side copying. Because the buffer was written by the device, it must be synchronized for CPU access; using dma_sync_single_for_device() can leave stale data visible to the CPU on non-coherent systems.
